Brody and Samuel are organizing a car wash to raise money to buy new hockey sticks for their school's hockey team. The number of hockey sticks they will be able to purchase for the team depends on the number of cars they wash.

s = the number of hockey sticks Brody and Samuel will be able to purchase
c = the number of cars Brody and Samuel wash

Which of the variables is independent and which is dependent?

Brody and Samuel are organizing a car wash to raise money to buy new hockey sticks for their school's hockey team. The number of hockey sticks they will be able to purchase for the team depends on the number of cars they wash.

choices.html: s is the independent variable and c is the dependent variable

content.html:
There are two variables. One is called the independent variable and the other is called the dependent variable.
The variable whose value does not depend on the other variable is the independent variable. The variable whose value depends on the other variable is the dependent variable.

choices.html: s is the independent variable and c is the dependent variable
c is the independent variable and s is the dependent variable
s is the independent variable and c is the dependent variable
c is the independent variable and s is the dependent variable

content.html:
Start by finding the dependent variable.

Since the number of hockey sticks Brody and Samuel will be able to purchase depends on the number of cars they wash, the number of hockey sticks is the dependent variable. So, s is the dependent variable.

Since the number of cars Brody and Samuel wash does not depend on the number of hockey sticks they will be able to purchase, the number of cars is the independent variable. So, c is the independent variable.
